structure.title: Company Profile
structure.summary: Maruti Suzuki India Limited, established in 1981 and a subsidiary of Suzuki Motor Corporation since 2002, is India's market leader in passenger vehicles and largest PV exporter. SMC holds 58.28% equity. Shares trade on NSE and BSE. In FY 2024-25, total sales surpassed 2 million units for the second consecutive year. Manufacturing sites include Gurugram, Manesar, Kharkhoda, and Gujarat (via Suzuki Motor Gujarat, a wholly-owned subsidiary). R&D centres are in Rohtak and Gurugram. The company has zonal, regional, and area offices across India. Production capacity is about 2.6 million units annually. The text includes sales volume data for FY21-FY25, cumulative production milestones, export sales volumes, and mentions sales channels in India.

Sustainability efforts are detailed: lifecycle environmental footprint reduction, resource efficiency via Sho-Sho-Kei-Tan-Bi, circularity, solar capacity expansion, logistics decarbonization, water recycling, safety advancements, and value chain ESG integration. It highlights railway dispatches for vehicle distribution, reducing emissions and fuel use through in-plant railway sidings. It mentions GHG reduction efforts in the value chain via renewable energy at suppliers and dealers. Finally, it addresses circular economy contributions through end-of-life vehicle management, including design for recyclability and a joint venture for vehicle dismantling and recycling, with metrics on materials recovered.

structure.title: Railway Dispatch, GHG Reduction, and Circular Economy Initiatives
structure.summary: The page outlines the company's triple bottom line performance, focusing on railway dispatch expansion (two in-plant sidings with 750,000 annual capacity, including new facilities at Gujarat and Manesar), reducing carbon emissions through rail (24.3% of dispatches in FY25, target 35% by FY31, fuel and CO2 savings), and GHG reduction efforts in the value chain (renewable electricity, solar-powered dealer workshops, local sourcing). It also covers circular economy contributions: end-of-life vehicle management via the IMDS tool (over 92% recyclable, over 98% recoverable materials) and the MSTI joint venture for vehicle dismantling and recycling, which recovered 3,063 MT of steel and 249 MT of aluminium in FY25.

structure.title: Triple Bottom Line Performance: Resource Use and Waste Management
structure.summary: The page covers Maruti Suzuki's Triple Bottom Line performance, focusing on optimizing natural resource use through steel scrap inputs, yield improvement reducing steel consumption by over 5,000 MT, and industrial symbiosis where 100% scrap is sold to suppliers and 30% used by other industries. It highlights 3R practices in packaging, including a 32% reduction in packaging material for New DZire and ~34% reuse in KD exports, plus 2,370+ MT plastic recycled. Waste management details zero waste-to-landfill with 15,148 MT hazardous waste co-processed, 5,244 MT hazardous waste recycled, and 1,50,000 MT non-hazardous waste recycled. It also references UN SDGs, material issues, and value creation approach.

It also describes the Maruti Suzuki Vendor Conference 2024, assessment mechanisms, training, and results. Additionally, it highlights the DIGILIB knowledge-sharing platform for suppliers and dealers, and talent pool creation through a Tool and Die Engineering course and training facility.

structure.title: Customer-Centricity
structure.summary: The text covers Maruti Suzuki's value creation approach and statutory reports, highlighting triple bottom line performance, customer-centricity, and safety assessments across the value chain linked to UN SDGs. It addresses material issues of product safety, quality, innovation, and digitalisation, detailing vehicle safety ratings under BNCAP for Dzire and Baleno, standard active and passive safety features, and behavioral safety. It describes the HEARTECT platform using ultra and advanced high-tensile steel for structural rigidity, tensile strength benefits, and safety assessments for logistics providers, suppliers, and dealers. It also reports stakeholder capability development, training person-hours, and the percentage of high-tensile steel used in the All New Dzire.

structure.title: Employer of Choice
structure.summary: The text covers Triple Bottom Line Performance at Maruti Suzuki India Limited, focusing on employment practices, occupational health and safety, and comprehensive benefits. It details employee benefit expenses for FY'25 and FY'24, gender diversity initiatives including new women hires and a dedicated HR council, and a gender diversity trend showing female representation rising from 3.6% to 4.9%. It highlights safety measures such as a 3-tier safety committee with 125 meetings, workforce suggestions for safety improvement, and near-miss incidents reported. Social security and welfare measures include post-retirement medical benefits for 1,148 superannuated employees, low-interest housing loans for 3,077 employees, 289 flats booked, and rewards for 7,942 employee children. Health and well-being programs cover 12,298 employees and families using non-occupational health schemes, 16,963 free medical consultations, and 13,664 periodic health check-ups.

structure.title: Responsible Corporate Citizen
structure.summary: The text covers Triple Bottom Line Performance and Responsible Corporate Citizen initiatives, aligned with UN SDGs, focusing on community development, skill development, and road safety. It details CSR activities in 36 villages including health, education, water, sanitation, and common assets. Specific projects include a multispecialty hospital in Sitapur, Gujarat with a Cath lab serving 400+ villages and 125,000+ people; a school with 621 students; and initiatives near Kharkhoda facility such as new classrooms, solar units, libraries benefiting 19,000 people and 600+ students. Also covered are an anaemia reduction program targeting ~20,000 women and children, water ATMs serving 38,500+ people in 25 villages, 4,520 household toilets, promotion of Fermented Organic Manure with IARI, the e-Parivartan employee volunteering program with 3,100+ hours, and road safety efforts training 5.1 million+ people across 8 IDTRs and 23 RSKCs, plus 45 automated driving test tracks.

structure.title: Skill Development
structure.summary: The text details the Company's skill development initiatives aligned with India's Skill India mission. It notes over 18,000 youth trained in 137 supported Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and over 2,000 in three Japan-India Institute of Manufacturing (JIMs), with a fourth JIM being set up in Sonipat. JIMs provide state-of-the-art vocational training in technical and behavioural skills. The text highlights a high-voltage course at an ITI with a training kit, and a comprehensive electric vehicle training program for Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV) and Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicle (SHEV) systems, preparing automotive technicians. In FY 2024-25, 2,700 students were trained, and 130 ITIs introduced customized BEV and SHEV training programs.

structure.title: Digitalisation and Innovation
structure.summary: This text covers Maruti Suzuki's digitalisation and innovation initiatives, including customer experience platforms like Nexaverse and Arenaverse, the MS Chatbox with video conferencing, Smart Parking Solutions, and Maruti Suzuki Smart Finance, which disbursed over H50,000 Cr to 6.8 lakh customers. It details the Mobijoy app for driver behaviour improvement, the Maruti Suzuki Innovation Programme, Accelerator, Incubation Programme with NSRCEL, Nurture pre-incubation with IIM-C, Mobility Challenge with T-Hub, Intrapreneurship Challenge, FundRays investor readiness programme, and Innovation Fund investments in DaveAI and Amlgo Labs. It also lists start-ups onboarded as partners across AI, immersive tech, mobility, AGV/AMR, IoT, and cybersecurity.

structure.title: External Environment
structure.summary: The text covers India's economic conditions, including GDP growth and passenger vehicle market trends, along with the Company's efforts to expand exports, increase consumer base, optimize costs, and invest in capacity. It addresses climate change with a multi-powertrain decarbonization strategy and GHG risk management, the regulatory landscape and safety compliance, the competitive landscape and Suzuki collaboration, and changing customer preferences towards SUVs, CNG, and advanced technologies, detailing the Company's product and feature enhancements.

structure.title: Stakeholder Engagement
structure.summary: The text details Maruti Suzuki's stakeholder engagement approach, emphasizing collaboration with internal and external groups based on dependence, responsibility, and influence. It outlines engagement activities, frequencies, and channels for employees, customers, shareholders, suppliers, dealers, local communities, and government authorities. It identifies material operational and strategic issues affecting economic, social, and environmental performance. The document lists each stakeholder group's key queries, needs, and expectations—such as employee well-being, customer product quality, shareholder powertrain strategy, supplier ESG readiness, dealer SUV lineup, community sanitation, and government carbon footprint reduction—along with page references to the Company's responses.

structure.title: Material Topics
structure.summary: The text outlines the Company's material topics, identified through stakeholder engagement and revalidated via internal consultations. It details the prioritization of these topics based on importance to the organization and stakeholders, including focus areas with no adverse impacts. It lists eight stakeholder groups and presents a materiality matrix categorizing topics by economic, environmental, social, and governance dimensions. It explains the IIRC framework's capitals and mapping of material topics to the UN SDGs. For each material topic, it provides relevance, boundary, associated capitals, SDG alignment, and report location. Topics covered include emissions reduction, product safety, economic performance, business continuity, natural resource use, innovation, people development, road safety, water recycling, occupational health and safety, waste management, end-of-life vehicles, employment practices, labour relations, corporate governance, community development, cybersecurity, data privacy, sustainable supply chain, skill development, and human rights.

structure.title: Risk Management
structure.summary: The text outlines the Company's structured risk management process, overseen by the Risk Management Committee, which identifies and mitigates risks to achieve strategic objectives and sustainable growth. It details specific risks: supply disruption from disasters (with mitigation like supplier communication and localization), risks from increased scale of operations (mitigated by resource scaling, stakeholder collaboration, and digitalisation), regulatory compliance risks (addressed via IT-enabled controls and early warning systems), consumer and personal data safeguarding (through policies and technology), IT security (via SOC, sandboxing, and awareness programs), and future product development capacity (through skilling and retention). Each risk is linked to related material topics.

structure.title: Way Forward
structure.summary: The text outlines Maruti Suzuki's strategic measures for sustainable value creation across six areas. Business Development focuses on expanding product portfolios, manufacturing capacity, and networks, including SUVs, BEVs, ethanol flex-fuel, and CNG vehicles, digital marketing, and pre-owned car business. Technology emphasizes carbon footprint reduction with a targeted powertrain mix by FY 2030-31 (15% BEV, 25% hybrid, 35% CNG, 25% ethanol-blended), regulatory compliance, and Industry 4.0. Cost Competitiveness involves cost optimization, localisation, value engineering, and employee suggestion schemes. Capability Building enhances design, testing, talent development, and digital training. Sustainable Practices cover energy conservation, renewable energy expansion to 319 MWp solar by FY 2030-31, 85% recyclability, IMDS monitoring, vehicle scrappage, 3R principles, green logistics, water recycling, health and safety, community development, and governance. Risk Management ensures business continuity, supplier excellence, talent retention, cybersecurity, and data security.

structure.title: Alignment with Sustainable Development Goals
structure.summary: The text outlines the company's alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, covering road safety initiatives (driver training, first-responder training, automated test tracks), health and well-being programs (community hospital, anaemia reduction, employee healthcare), education and vocational training (school, ITI support, apprenticeships), gender diversity, water stewardship (recycling, rainwater harvesting, water ATMs, sanitation), renewable energy (solar expansion), fair employment practices (code of conduct, safety, human rights), livelihood opportunities (Learn and Earn scheme), infrastructure and innovation (R&D, start-up programs), housing and transport affordability, sustainable consumption (3R practices, recycling), and climate action (hybrid/CNG technologies, rail transport, biogas).

structure.title: ESG Performance
structure.summary: The text covers Maruti Suzuki India Limited's ESG performance, detailing its commitment to responsible growth and sustainable value creation by integrating environmental, social, and governance considerations into business strategy. It highlights environmental initiatives like solar power capacity (78.2 MWp) and water recycling (~63%), social metrics such as 100% return to work rate, CSR spending (H 1,585 Mn), employee volunteering hours (~3,000), and governance aspects including 3 women directors, 4/7 independent directors on the sustainability committee, and GHG emissions avoided (0.18 Mn tCO2e) from railway-dispatched vehicles. It also presents key ESG milestones and forward-looking goals.

structure.title: Environment
structure.summary: MSIL's environmental commitment covers ISO 14001 certification, energy efficiency and renewable expansion (solar capacity, green tariff, biogas pilot), GHG emissions management, and energy-saving initiatives. It details ozone-depleting substance phase-out, water management with zero liquid discharge and canal water sourcing, and waste management via 3R principles and zero waste-to-landfill. Biodiversity efforts include Miyawaki plantation and water lagoons. The value chain section addresses green procurement, supplier environmental management system adoption, capacity building through MACE, dry wash adoption at workshops, and green logistics with rail dispatch expansion.

structure.title: ~0.52 Mn
structure.summary: The text covers Maruti Suzuki's environmental sustainability initiatives in FY 2024-25. It highlights rail transport reducing emissions, with 0.52 million vehicles transported and 0.18 million tCO2e avoided, and 99%+ of imported containers moved by rail. Rail mode's share of dispatches grew from 11.6% to 24.4%. The company emphasizes green products, including S-CNG, Smart Hybrid, and Strong Hybrid vehicles, and unveiled its first BEV, the e VITARA, with over 500 km range and ADAS. It launched S-CNG variants of the Swift and Dzire with high fuel efficiency. Cumulative CO2 avoidance from CNG and hybrid vehicles is detailed. End-of-life vehicle management via MSTI scrapped 6,468 vehicles, and 26 tonnes of Li-ion batteries were recycled. Overall, it summarizes efforts across the product lifecycle to reduce environmental impact.

structure.title: Social
structure.summary: The text covers MSIL's social initiatives: talent development, diversity, customer satisfaction, and CSR in education, healthcare, skill development, and environment. It details occupational health and safety with ISO 45001 certification, safety governance, training, performance data, campaigns, digitalization, value chain safety, and EV emergency preparedness. Human resources topics include diversity and inclusion, employee counts, POSH policy, welfare programs, listening framework, health and well-being, labour relations, wage equality, sustainability, talent acquisition and retention, supplier HR management, and learning and development for employees and value chain partners.

structure.title: Customer Satisfaction, Engagement and Support
structure.summary: The text covers Maruti Suzuki's customer-centric initiatives: digital engagement via AI chatbots, voice bots, WhatsApp, and virtual reality platforms (ARENAVERSE, NEXAVERSE); online dealership touchpoints; the Maruti Suzuki Smart Finance digital car financing platform with loan disbursement statistics; subscription-based mobility program details; service network expansion including touchpoints, NEXA workshops, Service-on-Wheels, mobile support, and Quick Response Teams; customer satisfaction measurement using NPS (score 89.5) and complaints per 1,000 vehicles (0.66); customer safety enhancements like six standard airbags and Bharat NCAP ratings; and product recall management with voluntary recalls and supplier quality support.

structure.title: Corporate Social Responsibility
structure.summary: Maruti Suzuki's CSR strategy ('focus, innovate, replicate') covers road safety (ADTTs), skill development (JIM, ITI support, tech courses), and community development. Key initiatives include Fermented Organic Manure promotion with IARI Pusa, school libraries in Haryana, and an anaemia reduction pilot. The Sitapur multispeciality hospital provides tertiary care to 400+ villages (125,000+ patients treated) and the Podar Learn School educates ~620 students with a 100% first-batch pass rate. Village development projects encompass water ATMs, pipelines, toilets, sewer lines, solar installations, bus sheds, community halls, and roads. A defect management framework with voluntary recalls is also described, alongside CSR Committee monitoring and third-party impact assessments.

structure.title: Village Development Project Social Impact and Infrastructure Outputs
structure.summary: The page provides key outputs of the Village Development Project since inception across four social areas. Primary Healthcare covers renovating six health centers, providing medical equipment, and an anemia reduction project targeting about 20,000 women and children in Manesar and Rohtak. Water includes 28 Water ATMs serving over 38,500 households, about 20 km of pipelines, three water tanks, village waterworks, and pond rejuvenation. Sanitation and Hygiene lists 4,520 household toilets, four waste collection vans, household waste collection, about 56 km of sewer lines, a waste management plant, and a 4R storytelling project. Education supported around 50 schools with infrastructure and learning equipment including water tanks, toilet blocks, boundary walls, paving, greening, classrooms, electrical fittings, education equipment, and additional teachers. A community member testimonial praises paver blocks at Gaushala for improving cleanliness and accessibility.

structure.title: Common Community Assets
structure.summary: The text covers Maruti Suzuki's community development and skill initiatives: construction of bus sheds, community halls, paver roads, facilitation centres, cremation sheds, storm drain repairs, solar streetlights, and village parks; testimonials on improved health centres, classrooms, and libraries. It details the e-Parivartan employee volunteering programme with blood donation, sapling plantation, donations to elderly homes, Braille kits, wheelchairs, and STEM kits. Skill development includes Japan India Institute for Manufacturing (JIM) with vocational training, new JIM in Sonipat, short-term RPL and RTD programmes, upgradation of ITIs with skill labs and automotive skill enhancement centres, support to Tathagat ITI, apprenticeship and PM Internship schemes, and road safety initiatives through IDTRs and RSKCs training millions of drivers.

structure.title: ~5.1 Mn
structure.summary: The text highlights driver training statistics: 5.1 million drivers trained since inception and 320,000 during the reporting period through IDTRs and RSKCs. It describes Automated Driving Test Tracks (ADTTs) with high-definition cameras and analytics for transparent licensing, noting 45 ADTTs set up across Delhi, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttar Pradesh, scaling from a 2017 Delhi pilot. Trainee testimonials emphasize improved confidence, fairness, and road safety awareness. Maruti Suzuki's holistic road safety approach integrates training, testing, enforcement via ITSMS, and emergency care through First-Responder Training and ambulance donations. The company received numerous awards for CSR, road safety, and skill development initiatives.

structure.title: Governance

It details the Board's structure, committees, and diversity, alongside key policies. Compliance management, including the Compliance Committee and supplier governance framework, is highlighted, as are legal proceedings. The text also addresses the Code of Business Conduct, whistleblower mechanism, intellectual property, data protection, information security, and value chain governance, including supplier assessments and sustainability initiatives. nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The text covers India's FY 2024-25 economic environment, including inflation, GDP growth, and monetary/fiscal policies. It details the passenger vehicle industry's performance, segment shares, and powertrain mix shifts. Maruti Suzuki's achievements are highlighted: record production and sales, export milestones, financial performance, and strategic initiatives like new plants and BEV preparation. Domestic sales include new model launches, marketing efforts, and customer profile changes. The text also covers CNG and hybrid vehicle growth, network expansion, digital initiatives, and the LCV segment. Exports show significant growth with new market entries. Service network expansion, warranty enhancements, digital tools, and aftermarket parts strategies are discussed.

nodes.title: Operations
nodes.summary: The text covers the company's operational achievements in FY 2024-25, including record production of over 2 million vehicles, managing complexity from 18 models and 650 variants across 100 export markets, and adapting to volatile domestic demand and shifting preferences. It highlights agile manufacturing, workforce upskilling, quality management enhancements, and use of Industry 4.0/5.0 technologies. A capacity expansion roadmap to 4 million units by FY 2030-31 is outlined, with recent increases at Manesar and a new Kharkhoda plant. The text also details conservation of natural resources and environmental protection efforts: resource efficiency via Suzuki's 'Sho-Sho-Kei-Tan-Bi' philosophy, design for recycling (92% recyclable, 98% recoverable), renewable energy expansion (78.2 MWp solar, 16% renewable electricity), 3R practices (100% metal scrap recycling, 100% water recycling), vehicle scrapping unit, packaging plastic reduction, and Extended Producer Responsibility. It mentions environmental compliance, supplier audits, IMDS tool for substances of concern, zero waste to landfill, and plans to increase solar capacity to 319 MWp by FY 2030-31.

nodes.title: Safety
nodes.summary: The text covers the Company's safety culture, governance via a three-tier committee system, and frontline engagement with over 248,000 safety suggestions and 1,224 near-misses reported. It details training for 94.6% of the workforce, Safety Month initiatives, supplier engagement, and a mobile app for road safety. It also addresses quality assurance, including the zero-defect philosophy, integrated Quality Management System, and developments like new Swift and Dzire launches, e VITARA validation, cybersecurity readiness, and exports. Quality management programs using the 4M approach (Man, Machine, Material, Method) are also mentioned, with Man and Machine aspects highlighted.

nodes.title: A) Introducing Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV)
nodes.summary: The text announces the Company's first Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV), the e VITARA, unveiled at the Bharat Mobility Expo in FY 2024-25. It highlights that e VITARA is Suzuki Motor Corporation's first BEV, with the Company serving as the global manufacturing hub for the Suzuki Group and planning exports to over 100 countries, boosting 'Make in India'. The Company aims to become India's largest BEV manufacturer within the first year of production. Suzuki Motor Corporation has committed significant R&D investment, with plans to launch four BEV models in India by FY 2030-31, aiming to be India's largest BEV OEM in production, domestic, and export sales. Additionally, the Company's powertrain strategy includes multiple carbon reduction technologies to cover the entire fleet, with a chart showing targets for various powertrain technologies as a percentage of overall Passenger Vehicle sales volume in India by FY 2030-31. The e VITARA, Maruti Suzuki's first Electric SUV, was unveiled by Mr. Toshihiro Suzuki and Mr. Hisashi Takeuchi at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025 in New Delhi.

nodes.summary: The page discusses three alternative fuel technologies. First, Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicles (SHEV) reduce carbon emissions without charging infrastructure, with the company offering SHEV in Grand Vitara and Invicto, showing improved fuel efficiency and growing sales. Second, Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) powertrain technology is promoted, with 14 CNG variants across 18 models; CNG vehicles constituted one in three domestic sales in FY 2024-25, with increasing contribution over years, benefiting customers, environment, and government. Third, biofuels including Compressed Biogas (CBG) and Ethanol-based Flex-fuel Vehicles (FFV) are explored; the company displayed India's first mass-segment flex-fuel prototype Wagon R FFV, capable of running on 20-85% ethanol blends, reducing carbon emissions by ~79% versus gasoline. E20 is prioritized, and all petrol models are E20 compatible.

nodes.title: E) Reducing Carbon Footprint by Enhancing Fuel Efficiency of IC Engine Vehicles
nodes.summary: The text covers Maruti Suzuki's initiatives to reduce carbon footprint through improved fuel efficiency of IC engine vehicles using a new Z-series powertrain, with fuel efficiency improvements in the Dzire. It details the Rohtak R&D Centre for regulatory compliance, supply chain management including ESG performance, supplier assessments, and governance frameworks. It discusses cost optimization efforts, logistics improvements via increased rail transport and fleet modernization, driver training, and financial performance including profit and loss, ratios, treasury operations, internal controls, and foreign exchange risk management. nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text discusses the Passenger Vehicle industry's slowdown in FY 2024-25, with low single-digit growth expected in FY 2025-26, and declining first-time buyer participation due to affordability challenges. Car penetration in India is low (~30 per 1,000 people), with over 88% of households excluded from safer transport access, highlighting social equity gaps. The entry-car segment has seen a 70% price surge since FY 2018-19 due to regulatory changes, and reviving it is vital for mass-market growth. The company aims to partner in India's Viksit Bharat 2047 goal, focusing on expanding product and market segments, enhancing features and technologies, and nearly doubling annual manufacturing capacity to 4 million units by FY 2030-31. It remains the largest PV exporter for four years with ~43% share, supported by Suzuki Motor Corporation, and aims to more than double export volumes, resume exports to advanced economies with its first BEV, and increase consumer base through diversification in segments, form-factors, and powertrains (BEVs, SHEVs, CNG, CBG, ethanol) to maximize decarbonization impact, with reference to targeted powertrain mix by FY 2030-31.
